name: Ohitashi (Japanese Blanched Greens With Savory Broth)

ingredients.name: soy sauce, preferably usukuchi soy sauce

instructions.primary_message: Prepare an ice bath in a large bowl. In a medium or large pot of salted boiling water, cook greens until tender, 1 to 2 minutes depending on type. Immediately transfer to prepared ice bath to cool.

Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, bring mirin and soy sauce to a simmer over medium-high heat, then remove from heat. Combine soy mixture with 3/4 cup dashi. Taste, then add more of remaining dashi if a more dilute flavor is desired. Let cool completely.

Drain greens. Using your hands, wring out as much water from greens as possible, then transfer to a container, pour dashi marinade on top, and toss to coat. Refrigerate, covered, for at least 30 minutes and up to 8 hours.

Arrange greens on a single serving plate or several individual ones; they are often arranged in a neat line, or compressed into a cylinder shape, though loosely mounding them also works. Drizzle some of the dashi marinade on top, then garnish with bonito flakes or sesame seeds. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: Asian, easy, green, leafy green, make ahead, side dish, spinach, vegetable, watercress

description: Ohitashi is a simple, light, and deeply flavorful Japanese side dish of blanched greens in a soy-based marinade. Make it ahead, then have it ready for the table with no additional effort.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr.

Optional or for serving: Bonito flakes or sesame seeds, for garnish

Optional substitutions: homemade dashi → instant dashi

Notes: Many kinds of leafy greens can work here, but make sure to avoid baby spinach, which becomes far too soft and squishy when cooked.
author: Daniel Gritzer
